creative-brainstorming.label: Creative brainstorming
creative-brainstorming.description: Wide-open idea generation, no constraints yet.
creative-brainstorming.skillsNeeded: Needs people comfortable generating and building on ideas quickly: Intuition for spotting new possibilities, Perceiving for staying open before locking in too early, and enough Extraversion in the room to keep energy and momentum going.

idealTypeReasons.ENFP: Their natural enthusiasm for new possibilities keeps the group generating fresh angles, and their genuine interest in people means even the wildest ideas get built on rather than shut down.
idealTypeReasons.ENTP: They thrive on questioning assumptions and testing an idea out loud, which is exactly the friction that pushes a rough concept somewhere more interesting.
idealTypeReasons.INFP: Their strong internal sense of what feels meaningful surfaces ideas the rest of the room would not have thought to explore, even if they need a little space to voice them.
idealTypeReasons.INTP: Their comfort taking a concept apart to see how it actually works means the group's ideas get stress-tested for logic, not just enthusiasm.

creative-brainstorming.excelsAt: A group built from these types moves fast between ideas, plays well off each other's tangents, and rarely runs out of new angles to explore. The risk is polish: without someone willing to eventually narrow the list down, the ideas can stay ideas.

process-brainstorming.label: Process brainstorming
process-brainstorming.description: Improving or fixing something that already exists.
process-brainstorming.skillsNeeded: Needs people who can take a known problem and actually land on a workable fix: Sensing for staying grounded in what's really happening, and Judging for turning ideas into a concrete next step rather than leaving them open-ended.

idealTypeReasons.ISTJ: Their instinct to verify what's actually happening before proposing a fix keeps the group anchored to the real problem instead of a guessed one.
idealTypeReasons.ESTJ: Their bias toward a concrete next step turns a discussion about what's broken into an actual assigned fix.
idealTypeReasons.ISFJ: Their attentiveness to the practical details others overlook means the fix accounts for how the process affects the people using it.
idealTypeReasons.ESFJ: Their read on how a change will land with the team helps the group choose a fix people will actually adopt, not just tolerate.

process-brainstorming.excelsAt: A group like this stays grounded in what's actually broken and pushes toward a fix that will hold up in practice, not just on paper. The risk is getting so anchored to how things currently work that a genuinely better approach gets overlooked.

strategic-planning.label: Strategic planning
strategic-planning.description: Setting direction and prioritizing what's next.
strategic-planning.skillsNeeded: Needs people who can see where things are headed and commit to a direction: Intuition for spotting the bigger picture and what it implies down the road, and Judging for actually deciding and locking in a plan rather than exploring indefinitely.

idealTypeReasons.INTJ: Their comfort building long-range plans several moves ahead means the group's direction holds up under scrutiny, not just optimism.
idealTypeReasons.ENTJ: Their decisiveness turns open-ended discussion into a committed direction, and their drive keeps the group moving once it's set.
idealTypeReasons.INFJ: Their instinct for spotting the pattern behind a situation surfaces implications the rest of the group would only notice much later.
idealTypeReasons.ENFJ: Their ability to rally people around a shared direction means the plan lands as something the team actually believes in, not just a document.

strategic-planning.excelsAt: A group like this sees several moves ahead and is comfortable committing to a direction rather than endlessly revisiting it. The risk is moving too fast past the people who'll actually have to execute the plan day to day.

data-analysis.label: Data & analysis
data-analysis.description: Digging into numbers, patterns, and root causes.
data-analysis.skillsNeeded: Needs people who can sit with numbers and draw a sound conclusion: Thinking for objective, logic-first reasoning, Sensing for staying with what the data actually shows rather than assumptions, and enough Introversion to focus deeply without needing constant interaction.

idealTypeReasons.ISTJ: Their patience for verifying detail before drawing a conclusion keeps the group from mistaking a coincidence for a finding.
idealTypeReasons.INTJ: Their instinct to keep questioning a conclusion until the logic holds up means weak analysis gets caught before it goes anywhere.
idealTypeReasons.ISTP: Their hands-on, troubleshoot-in-the-moment approach makes them quick to spot where the data or the method doesn't add up.
idealTypeReasons.INTP: Their genuine enjoyment of taking a problem apart means they will keep digging past the first plausible explanation.

data-analysis.excelsAt: A group like this is comfortable sitting with a problem until the numbers actually make sense, and won't take a conclusion at face value without checking it. The risk is spending so long validating the data that a decision never actually gets made.

operational.label: Operational execution
operational.description: Turning a plan into consistent, reliable delivery.
operational.skillsNeeded: Needs people who turn plans into steady execution: Sensing for practical, on-the-ground detail, and Judging for structure and follow-through. Thinking and Feeling both work here, depending on whether the work is more process-heavy or more people-heavy.

idealTypeReasons.ISTJ: Their quiet, consistent follow-through means commitments made in planning actually get delivered.
idealTypeReasons.ESTJ: Their organizational instinct turns a plan into a clear chain of accountability, so nothing falls through the gaps.
idealTypeReasons.ISFJ: Their attention to practical, on-the-ground detail keeps execution grounded in what's actually happening day to day.
idealTypeReasons.ESFJ: Their focus on keeping the team coordinated and supported means delivery stays steady even when the work gets repetitive.

operational.excelsAt: A group like this delivers what it commits to, on schedule, without much drama. The risk is rigidity: once the plan is set, this kind of group can be slow to adjust when the situation genuinely changes.

quality-review.label: Quality review
quality-review.description: Catching errors and making sure nothing's missed.
quality-review.skillsNeeded: Needs people with a sharp eye for what's wrong or missing: Sensing for catching concrete detail, and a strong pull toward Judging, since this kind of work has little tolerance for leaving things open-ended or half-checked.

idealTypeReasons.ISTJ: Their thoroughness and low tolerance for leaving something half-checked means little slips through unnoticed.
idealTypeReasons.ISFJ: Their careful, detail-oriented nature catches the small inconsistencies a faster read would miss.
idealTypeReasons.ESTJ: Their insistence on a clear standard and follow-through means the group holds the line rather than letting good-enough slide.

quality-review.excelsAt: A group like this catches what everyone else missed and rarely lets something half-finished slide through. The risk is that the bar can get so high that good-enough work gets held back longer than it needs to be.

client-facing.label: Client-facing
client-facing.description: Working directly with clients or stakeholders.
client-facing.skillsNeeded: Needs people comfortable reading and responding to others: Feeling for empathy and rapport, and enough Extraversion to carry a conversation and build trust. Sensing or Intuition both work, depending on whether the client wants concrete answers or big-picture vision.

idealTypeReasons.ESFJ: Their genuine attentiveness to what people need makes clients feel looked after, not just managed.
idealTypeReasons.ENFJ: Their ability to read a room and speak to what matters to the client builds trust quickly and keeps the relationship personal.
idealTypeReasons.ESFP: Their warmth and ease in the moment make clients comfortable being direct, which surfaces real concerns earlier.
idealTypeReasons.ENFP: Their genuine curiosity about people and enthusiasm for possibility helps clients feel heard while staying excited about where things are headed.

client-facing.excelsAt: A group like this builds trust quickly and makes the people on the other side of the table feel genuinely heard. The risk is over-promising, or softening bad news the client actually needs to hear.

sales-pitching.label: Sales & pitching
sales-pitching.description: Persuading and building excitement for an idea.
sales-pitching.skillsNeeded: Needs people who can build excitement and sell a vision: Extraversion for carrying the energy of a pitch, Intuition for painting the bigger possibility rather than just listing facts, and enough Feeling to read how the room is responding.

idealTypeReasons.ENFP: Their natural enthusiasm for a big idea makes the vision feel exciting rather than rehearsed.
idealTypeReasons.ENTP: Their quick wit and comfort debating on the fly means they can adapt the pitch the moment the room pushes back.
idealTypeReasons.ESFP: Their energy and presence make a pitch feel alive, and they read the room's reaction as it happens.
idealTypeReasons.ESTP: Their comfort acting on incomplete information means they close with conviction instead of hedging.

sales-pitching.excelsAt: A group like this brings energy and conviction that's hard to fake, and adapts the pitch on the fly based on how the room is reacting. The risk is getting ahead of the details the buyer will eventually ask about.

conflict-resolution.label: People & conflict resolution
conflict-resolution.description: Mediating tension and giving hard feedback fairly.
conflict-resolution.skillsNeeded: Needs people who can mediate fairly: Feeling for genuine empathy toward everyone involved, balanced with enough Thinking to stay objective rather than just smoothing things over to keep the peace.

idealTypeReasons.ENFJ: Their instinct to encourage growth in people means they can push through a hard conversation while keeping people invested in a good outcome.
idealTypeReasons.ISFJ: Their genuine loyalty and quiet attentiveness make people on both sides feel their side is actually being heard.
idealTypeReasons.INFJ: Their sensitivity to underlying tension means they often see the real issue underneath the stated disagreement.
idealTypeReasons.ESFJ: Their instinct to keep the group cohesive drives them to actually close the tension out rather than let it fester.

conflict-resolution.excelsAt: A group like this can sit with tension without rushing to smooth it over, and tends to leave people feeling fairly heard on both sides. The risk is prioritizing harmony over actually naming the hard truth that needs to be said.

crisis.label: Crisis response
crisis.description: Reacting fast and adapting under real pressure.
crisis.skillsNeeded: Needs people who can decide quickly under pressure: Thinking for fast, logical calls, Sensing for reading the real situation in front of them rather than theorizing, and Perceiving for adapting as things keep changing.

idealTypeReasons.ESTP: Their comfort acting on real-time information rather than waiting for a full picture means they respond while it still matters.
idealTypeReasons.ISTP: Their calm, hands-on troubleshooting keeps them effective when the situation is changing faster than anyone can fully explain it.
idealTypeReasons.ESTJ: Their decisiveness under pressure means someone is always ready to call the next step rather than let the group freeze.

crisis.excelsAt: A group like this stays calm, reads the real situation fast, and acts without waiting for perfect information. The risk is moving so quickly that longer-term consequences don't get enough consideration.
